checks: Checked source §6. The finite cost assumes finitely many values, so its selected essential infimum is a value on a positive π-mass set. The exact double-unused-endpoint condition gives the almost-everywhere upper bound on the product of the unused measures.

Open-cap cost is lower semicontinuous since all weights are nonnegative. A violation on the support product would give an open product neighborhood of positive unused product measure, contrary to the almost-everywhere bound.

The unused measures are dominated by Lebesgue volume. Their compact supports therefore have volumes at least l,s. Brunn–Minkowski applies to these compact sets without convexity, and compatibility puts their average in B. Removing finitely many Lebesgue-null cutting planes equates open and closed costs in the volume estimate.
